about: The priest asks God to make the offering blessed, acknowledged, approved, spiritual and acceptable. The final petition asks that it may become for us the Body and Blood of God's most beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

s01.translation: Be pleased, O God, we pray, to make this offering in every respect

s02.narrative: The priest makes three signs of the cross over the offerings.

s03.translation: blessed, acknowledged, approved, spiritual and acceptable:

s04.narrative: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the Host alone, at the word Corpus, and one over the chalice alone, at Sanguis.

s05.translation: so that it may become for us the Body and Blood of Your most beloved Son,

w001.function: A relative pronoun agreeing with “oblatiónem” in the preceding prayer.

w003.function: The expressed subject pronoun, which Latin usually omits, emphasizes the addressee named immediately as “Deus” (w004).

w017.function: Nominative. “Corpus” and “Sanguis” are predicate nominatives with “fiat” (w020). The understood subject is the “oblátio” introduced at the beginning of the prayer, so the verb is singular.

w020.function: The present subjunctive of “fio”, here: “may it become”.
